title: Battle of Ain Jalut
summary: On 3 September 1260 a Mamluk army sent from Egypt under Sultan Qutuz, with Baybars commanding its vanguard, defeated the Mongol force of Kitbuqa at the spring of Ain Jalut in the Jezreel Valley. The victory halted the Mongol advance into Syria and Palestine and left the Mamluks controlling the region from Egypt to the Euphrates.

where.modern_name: Well of Harod (Ain Jalut spring), Jezreel Valley, northern Israel
where.historical_name: Ain Jalut (Ain Jalut), Jezreel Valley, Palestine, near Nazareth; Mamluk force from Egypt against a Mongol army serving Hulagu in Syria and Palestine

importance.justification: A Mamluk victory that stopped the Mongol advance into Syria and Palestine and shaped control of the region for the following decades.

sources.title: How the Mamluks Beat the Unstoppable Mongols at the Battle of Ain Jalut
Wikidata item Q603425 (Well of Harod), coordinate location (P625)

reviewer_note: Least sure of the exact site: the pin is the Well of Harod, which Wikidata lists as the spring; both sources place the battle at the spring of Ain Jalut in the Jezreel Valley. Sources disagree on Mongol numbers (EBSCO: no more than twenty thousand; TheCollector: around 12,000) and on whether Kitbuqa was captured and beheaded (EBSCO) or died fighting (TheCollector), so neither is stated.
